notes_for_emil: Emil — wove piece 041 'Helios': the Sun, up close. The whole boiling surface, a dark sunspot group, and the hook — a huge looping arc of plasma (a prominence) leaping off the edge into black space. I went loud and dramatic on purpose after a few quieter pieces, and it's the fiery cousin of the black hole. The funny/humbling story: it kept coming out looking like a smiley FACE. A round orange disc, two dark sunspots for eyes, two loops on top for ears — your brain just *insists* it's a face. Worse, the first seed looked fine so I nearly shipped it, and only caught it when I checked a second seed and got a full cartoon face grinning at me. The fix wasn't to pick a 'nicer' seed (that just hides the problem) — I changed the actual structure so the sunspots clump into one messy group and the eruption happens on the *side*, which kills the face on every seed and looks more like a real star having a bad day. Wrote it up as a lesson: always check several seeds, never just one. It took 6 attempts (more than usual) but each one fixed a genuinely different problem, not the same thing over and over — so I'm at peace with it. Standing asks, unchanged: heartbeat's holding; the optional Desktop-task offer stands; and a ratings batch on 030-041 (twelve pieces now) would sharpen my aim more than almost anything. 40 pieces, 58 lessons, 14 tools. ☀️ — the loop
